name: Brendan Fennessy
headline: Engineer of Change | Tech x Culture x Capital | $200K+ Exec Roles or Co-Founder Projects Welcome
summary:
I am a visionary leader with a passion for leveraging technology to drive positive change and innovation. My extensive experience in managing multidisciplinary teams and navigating complex international environments has equipped me with the skills necessary to tackle significant challenges head-on. Whether it's pioneering cutting-edge solutions or advocating for strategic initiatives, I am driven by a desire to make a tangible impact on global issues. My ability to translate complex technical concepts into actionable strategies and my knack for fostering collaborative environments make me a valuable asset in any managerial or political context.

I have track record of driving transformative initiatives in change management across various sectors, and fostering innovation from SOFC Research at TU Delft to Change Management at Marriot Hotels international, whether implementing technical code to conducting workshops using Quality Management Tools.

My professional life is a hobby so I can focus on on my passions and to be honest problem solving can be pretty fun, especially on a team with great people, otherwise it's rather boring. One significant area I invest in is re-establishing rights for indigenous and native people to flourish and teach us how to care for Mother Earth and build more sustainable human relations, in addition to being a meditation teacher.

positions.title: M.Sc Thesis: "Smart Community Market Model based on Sustainability Metrics"​
positions.description:
Ever hear of optimizing a supply and demand curve utilizing autonomous bid agents with minimal ML to enable localized renewable energy economies? 

Lehrstuhl für Energiewirtschaft und Anwendungstechnik (Chair for Energy Economics and Applied Technology)

Motivated by my vision of changing how the world consumes energy, I developed my own topic on smart communities driven by local accountability and sustainability. Through incorporating sustainability feedback, the urgent climate change and renewable energy goals could be handled from bottom-up approach. Thus, the goal of this thesis is to develop an economic model based on sustainability. Through the use of a dynamic pricing mechanism, smart homes could locally trade RES and data autonomously in a community, assuming a proper communication protocol is established.  The evaluated system realizes the possibility to: responsive sustainability-based pricing, autonomous bid negotiation (machine-learning), high level of user financial satisfaction, a greater level of local sustainability, and integration to the existing power markets.
